entities.summary: Giani Pritam Singh Dhillon was an Indian freedom fighter and Sikh missionary who, as a member of the Ghadar Party, was instrumental in the planning of the failed 1915 Ghadar conspiracy in the British Indian Army. Giani Pritam Singh Dhillon was a close friend of Gurbaksh Singh Dhillon, famous Sikh Indian independence movement leader and prominent member of the Indian National Army. He was also close associate of Subhas Chandra Bose. Pritam Singh is also remembered for reviving the same idea during World War II by seeking Japanese support in the establishment of what came to be the Indian National Army.

historicalSignificance.significanceNarrative: Giani Pritam Singh Dhillon's involvement in the Ghadar Party and his association with prominent figures like Gurbaksh Singh Dhillon and Subhas Chandra Bose contributed to the planning of the failed 1915 Ghadar conspiracy, which had significant regional impact on the Indian independence movement. His efforts during World War II to establish the Indian National Army with Japanese support further underscored his importance in shaping regional dynamics.
